science.title: Orionid meteor shower 2026: Date, peak time and how to watch one of the year's most beautiful meteor showers
science.description: Orionids meteor shower peaks in mid-October and is known for bright meteors visible in the night sky. The meteors originate from comet 1P/Halley, which sheds debris when it approaches the Sun. Observers are advised to find dark locations away from city lights to view the meteors effectively. The radiant for this shower is located just north of Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion.

science.title: Prolyl hydroxylation is required for maturation and secretion of Zika virus non-structural protein 1
science.description: Mosquito-borne orthoflaviviruses such as Zika virus (ZIKV) and dengue virus (DENV) have a high epidemic potential and are associated with a wide range of possible outcomes, from asymptomatic infections to severe complications. The orthoflavivirus non-structural protein 1 (NS1), which can be membrane-bound as well as secreted from the cell, plays important roles in viral replication, immune evasion, and pathogenesis. To describe the interactome of ZIKV NS1, we infected Huh7 and neural progenitor cells with a recombinant ZIKV expressing FLAG-tagged NS1 and identified interacting proteins by quantitative mass spectrometry. In both cell types, multiple prolyl hydroxylases, glycosylation enzymes, ER-associated degradation proteins, and proteins involved in immunity were identified as NS1 interactors. Mass spectrometry data showed that NS1 contains potential hydroxyproline residues, suggesting that prolyl hydroxylase enzymes are involved in post-translational modification of NS1. In agreement, chemical inhibition of prolyl hydroxylases impaired NS1 intracellular trafficking and plasma membrane localization and reduced ZIKV RNA levels and titers. Mutagenesis of the proline residue at position 281 impaired NS1 secretion, although viral replication was unaffected. Moreover, substituting proline at position 267 strongly dysregulated NS1 expression and reverted to the wild-type sequence already after a single passage, suggesting that this mutation leads to severe replication defects. Our results identify prolyl hydroxylation as an essential post-translational modification of ZIKV NS1.

science.title: Molecular architecture of Cryptococcus cell walls reveals species-specific chitosan-dependent remodeling
science.description: Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are fungal pathogens that cause life-threatening infections, including cryptococcal meningitis. A distinctive feature of the cryptococcal cell wall is the extensive deacetylation of chitin to chitosan, a modification that is essential for virulence but whose structural role in cell-wall organization remains poorly understood. Here, we analyze the cell walls of wild-type strains of both species and their avirulent chitosan-deficient mutants, which serve as vaccine candidates. Loss of chitosan disrupted cell morphology and altered cell-wall ultrastructure, with more pronounced defects in C. neoformans. Solid-state NMR reveals that aggregated α-(1→3)-glucans form the principal rigid domain of the cell wall in both species and are closely associated with chitin microfibrils, whereas surrounding β-glucans and mannoproteins constitute a more dynamic matrix. Chitosan modulates hydration and flexibility, and its loss increases chitin exposure and triggers species-specific remodeling of the polysaccharide network. In C. neoformans, chitosan depletion increased α-(1→3)-glucan content and reduced β-glucan levels, whereas C. gattii selectively lost one α-(1→3)-glucan subtype while maintaining β-glucan levels. Although capsule production remained intact, chitosan deficiency altered glucuronoxylomannan linkage patterns and mannoprotein composition. These findings reveal how chitosan organizes cryptococcal cell-wall architecture and highlight distinct structural adaptation strategies among pathogenic Cryptococcus species. This study reveals distinct cell-wall organization in two pathogenic Cryptococcus species, revealing that chitosan loss triggers species-specific structural remodeling that may influence host interactions.

science.title: Prevalence of 406 rare diseases by ethnicity and recorded COVID-19 infection rates among 62.5 million people in England
science.description: Rare diseases (RD) are individually uncommon but collectively affect millions of people. Yet national estimates of their prevalence, especially across ethnic groups, are limited, and how the COVID-19 pandemic affected people with RD across ethnic groups is unknown. We aimed to estimate the prevalence of 406 RD by ethnicity, and to describe recorded COVID-19 infection across these RD and ethnic groups, in England. We conducted a cross-sectional study within the National Health Service (NHS) England Secure Data Environment, accessed via the British Heart Foundation (BHF) Data Science Centre’s CVD-COVID-UK/COVID-IMPACT Consortium, linking primary care, hospital, and mortality records for individuals alive on 31 July 2023. We calculated age- and sex-standardised prevalence for 406 RD, and recorded COVID-19 infection rates for the overall group, for each RD, and across the six-group Office for National Statistics (ONS) and 19-group NHS ethnicity classifications. Of 62.5 million people, 1.05 million (1.7%) had at least one of the 406 RD. Recorded COVID-19 infection was higher in the RD group than in the non-RD population (32.8% vs. 29.0%). Within the RD group, infection rates varied by ethnicity (e.g. 27.7% in the Pakistani and 23.8% in the Black African groups, versus 33.7% in the White British group) and by specific RD (24.6–41.2% among the 25 most common). Age- and sex-standardised prevalence also varied widely across ethnic groups, with substantial heterogeneity emerging only when broad categories were disaggregated into the more granular NHS classifications (for example, markedly elevated discoid lupus erythematosus prevalence in Black Caribbean but not Black African individuals, obscured within the aggregate “Black” category). This national, ethnicity-resolved map shows that rare-disease prevalence varies substantially across ethnic groups, with differences largely hidden within broad categories, and that recorded COVID-19 infection among people with RD varied across ethnic groups, with the highest rates observed in the ONS White and NHS White British groups. These findings provide a baseline to support earlier, fairer diagnosis and more targeted care.

ai.title: Zen Technologies to acquire 52% stake in Cogknit for ₹135.15 crore
ai.description: Zen Technologies acquires 51.98% stake in Cogknit Semantics for ₹135.15 crore. Cogknit won iDEX challenge for Battlefield Management System and received Raksha Mantri’s Award. Deal includes primary subscription and secondary purchase; Ashish Kacholia also invests. Cogknit turnover declined from ₹2.24 crore in FY24 to ₹0.48 crore in FY26. Acquisition aligns with Zen’s Samvid AI platform for shared battlefield awareness.
